subsystems.name: Luminescent core
subsystems.role: produces visible light through a biochemical or polymer reaction.
parts: luciferase enzyme (e.g. from fireflies or bacteria)
cofactors such as ATP and oxygen

subsystems.name: Biosensing module
subsystems.role: detects a specific internal marker or electrical signal and triggers light emission.

subsystems.name: Encapsulation and delivery
subsystems.role: protects the active components from immune attack and places them in the dermis.

subsystems.name: Dermal interface
subsystems.role: keeps the ink stable and supplied with nutrients inside living skin.
parts: vascular access for glucose and oxygen

subsystems.name: Energy supply
subsystems.role: provides the chemical energy needed for repeated light emission.

subsystems.name: Optical readout
subsystems.role: captures the faint glow through skin for display or health monitoring.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the sensing–luminescence circuit
buildSteps.detail: Design a genetic or biochemical switch that links a chosen biomarker (such as glucose or pH) to the production of light.

buildSteps.title: Produce the luminescent proteins
buildSteps.detail: Culture cells that express luciferase, or synthesise a bioluminescent polymer in the lab.

buildSteps.title: Formulate the ink
buildSteps.detail: Mix the active components with a carrier fluid that can be injected into skin without losing activity.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate for immune evasion
buildSteps.detail: Coat the payload in hydrogels or lipid shells that let small molecules in but keep immune cells out.

buildSteps.title: Apply to the dermis
buildSteps.detail: Use a microneedle patch or modified tattoo machine to deposit the ink at a consistent depth.

buildSteps.title: Validate the signal in vivo
buildSteps.detail: Test in animal skin to confirm that the glow appears only when the target marker is present and is visible through the skin.

buildSteps.title: Refine for long-term stability
buildSteps.detail: Adjust the formulation so the ink keeps working for months or years despite skin turnover and UV exposure.

prerequisites.why: luciferase and luciferin are well-understood and already used in research imaging.

prerequisites.tech: Gene delivery or cell encapsulation in skin
prerequisites.why: some skin gene therapies are in trials, but no method yet gives durable, safe expression in the dermis.
implantable glucose sensors exist, but none are integrated with a light-emitting tattoo.

prerequisites.tech: Long-term stability of biomolecules in skin
prerequisites.why: proteins and nucleic acids degrade in living tissue; no ink yet maintains function for years.
pulse oximetry works, but detecting a faint bioluminescent glow under skin is harder.

pathway.milestone: lab demonstrations of colour-changing tattoos that respond to pH or glucose
pathway.unlocks: proof that skin can host a working biosensor.

pathway.milestone: bioluminescent tattoos that glow in response to a marker in animal skin
pathway.unlocks: a visible signal without external power or electronics.

pathway.milestone: human trials for medical monitoring, such as a tattoo that glows when blood sugar is low
consumer aesthetic tattoos with programmable colours or patterns
pathway.unlocks: dynamic body art controlled by the wearer or by internal state.

pathway.milestone: integration with wearables for closed-loop health management
pathway.unlocks: automatic alerts or drug delivery triggered by the tattoo's glow.
